newsitem.title: USA: Minor Metals lose one cobalt case, another pending.
newsitem.headline: Minor Metals lose one cobalt case, another pending.

text.p: Judge T. S. Ellis of U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia on Tuesday dismissed the case regarding the February sale of stockpiled cobalt brought by Minor Metals Inc against the Defense National Stockpile Center, a court official said.
"The complaint is dismissed," the official said. The temporary restraining order which had been granted by the Virginia court to Minor Metals was scrapped.
Judge Ellis said the remaining 135,000 lbs of cobalt, the balance of undistributed material from the negotiated sale of 1.1 million lbs in February, could now be delivered to the buyers.
Minor Metals' legal counsel and Stockpile officials were not immediately available for comment Wednesday.

However, on Tuesday, prior to the decision, Minor Metals' attorney, David Dempsey of law firm Piper & Marbury, said no further sales of stockpiled cobalt could go ahead until a separate case in the Court of Federal Claims, scheduled for May 15, was heard.
To date, Stockpile's sale of around one million lbs of cobalt in March and April, respectively, were put on hold pending the outcome of the two parallel court cases.
In the Court of Federal Claims, Minor Metals has complained principally that Stockpile's insistence on the lack of an "all or none" clause in bids was anti-competitive.
